paper_metadata.title: The value of 24-hour video-EEG in evaluating recurrence risk following a first unprovoked seizure: A prospective study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study describes the source population and recruitment period clearly. However, it is a single-center study at a tertiary hospital (West China Hospital), which may introduce referral bias. The participation rate of eligible individuals is not explicitly stated, making it difficult to assess if the sample is truly representative of all first-seizure patients in the community.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Clinic patients or outpatients who had experienced a single first unprovoked seizure were recruited from the West China Hospital of Sichuan University between January 2010 and January 2013.
items.reasoning: The authors specify the setting (tertiary hospital) and the clinical condition (first unprovoked seizure).

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Consecutively 134 patients with a first unprovoked epileptic seizure were recuited from West China Hospital
items.reasoning: While 'consecutive' recruitment is mentioned, the referral patterns to this specific hospital are not detailed, which is relevant for a tertiary center.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between January 2010 and January 2013.
items.reasoning: The dates are clearly defined.

items.evidence_snippet: West China Hospital, West China Medical School, Sichuan University, 17th, Wai Nan Guo Xue Lane, Chengdu 610041, China

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The diagnostic criteria for seizure were according to those formulated by the ILAE in 2005 [1]. ... Patients were excluded from our study if their first paroxysmal events were non-epileptic seizures, acute symptomatic seizures...
items.reasoning: Detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria based on ILAE standards are provided, including a flowchart.

items.evidence_snippet: sex, age, location, history of alcohol and tobacco use, marital status, educational level and profession, seizure type, presence/absence of nocturnal seizure, and any detrimental items in the medical history

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study reports a clear follow-up strategy and ensures a minimum 24-month follow-up for those without recurrence. The use of survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier) appropriately handles censored data.

items.reasoning: The study implies all 134 recruited patients were followed until recurrence or the 24-month mark.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary prognostic factor (24-hour VEEG) is well-defined, measured using a standardized protocol, and interpreted by experts blinded to the study objectives.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: A 24-hour VEEG (EBNeuro S.p.A, Germany) was recorded for each patient within 7 days after the first unprovoked seizure. We used 24-channel digital recordings (international standard 10/20 system)...
items.reasoning: The measurement tool, duration, and timing are precisely defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Two EEG experts who were blinded to the study analyzed the 24-hour VEEG results.
items.reasoning: Blinding of the assessors and use of experts enhances reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: The VEEG recordings were classified as either normal or abnormal. An abnormal VEEG was further categorized as either (a) non-epileptiform discharges... or (b) epileptiform discharges
items.reasoning: The categorization follows standard clinical neurological practice.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All patients underwent VEEG and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain
items.reasoning: The protocol was applied consistently to the entire cohort.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: The interictal VEEG was normal in 58 patients (43.3%) and abnormal in 76 (47.7%) patients.
items.reasoning: VEEG data appears to be available for all 134 participants.

items.label: Method used for missing data

items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There is no mention of missing PF data or imputation, suggesting complete data collection.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure recurrence) is clearly defined, but its measurement relies on patient/witness report, which is subject to recall bias. While this is standard in epilepsy research, it is less objective than the PF measurement.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: If a seizure recurred, the follow-up was ceased... ensuring that the shortest follow-up time was at least 2 years.
items.reasoning: Recurrence is the clear endpoint, with a defined minimum follow-up.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The patients came to our outpatient clinic at follow-up times... We attempted to maintain contact with patients by phone or letter
items.reasoning: Outcome measurement relies on clinical interview and self-reporting, which is standard but carries inherent risk of under-reporting or misclassification.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The patients came to our outpatient clinic at follow-up times of 3, 6, 12, and 24 months
items.reasoning: A standardized follow-up schedule was applied to all.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study measured a wide range of potential confounders (age, MRI, medical history) and used multivariable Cox regression to adjust for these factors, finding VEEG to be an independent predictor.

items.reasoning: Expert review of imaging ensures reliable measurement of structural confounders.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: agreed not to receive anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs) treatment until seizure recurrence.
items.reasoning: The design controlled for the confounding effect of AED treatment on recurrence risk.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: multivariate analysis using the Cox regression model determined that only an abnormal VEEG was a statistically significant predictor
items.reasoning: Multivariable adjustment was performed to isolate the effect of the VEEG.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods (Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression) are appropriate for time-to-event data. Results are reported transparently with RRs and 95% CIs.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Survival analysis was performed using Kaplan-Meier survival curves. The COX proportional hazard model was used in univariate analyses.
items.reasoning: The analytical plan is standard and well-described.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: We used the chi-square test (T test) and logistics to evaluate whether relative risk factors were predictive factors for seizure recurrence in the bivariate analyses.
items.reasoning: The authors used bivariate screening followed by multivariable modeling.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: The overall accumulated risks of recurrence were 8.2%, 16.4%, 29.9%, 46.3%, and 51.5% at 3, 6, 12, 24 and over 24 months
items.reasoning: Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier are the gold standards for prognosis studies involving follow-up time.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
